clue.text: Artists apply to notorious preacher

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, so artists are RAs
to apply, as for a job, is to put in

explanation.surface: Painters lend their skills to a scandalous preacher, perhaps for a portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasputin was the infamous Russian mystic and holy man who held sway over the last Tsar's family.

clue.text: Ileum's the better for digesting it

definitions.text: Ileum's the better for digesting it

indicators.note: digesting breaks food down and reworks it, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: the word taken letter by letter, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A health tip: your gut is better off for digesting this.
explanation.walkthrough: The ileum is part of the small intestine; the whole clue is both wordplay and a description of the fibrous breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a fibre-rich breakfast cereal reputed to help the bowels, so the gut benefits from digesting it.

clue.text: 'Omo sapiens replaces one in cape, an oriental fiend

indicators.note: replaces says one piece is swapped out of the word and another put in its place

blocks.note: a fichu is a small triangular shawl or cape worn round the shoulders
the Roman numeral for one
Homo sapiens is the human, here with its H dropped as the apostrophe shows

explanation.surface: A mock-scientific note on a caped Eastern villain, in a dropped-aitch accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Omo marks a dropped H, so the human becomes 'UMAN, which takes the place of I in FICHU.
explanation.definitionFit: Fu Manchu is Sax Rohmer's sinister Chinese master criminal, a stock villain of early pulp thrillers.

clue.text: Mounted study maintaining "Two Gentlemen" premieres appeared before "Macbeth"

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the thing that appeared

indicators.note: in a down entry, something mounted is raised up, so the word reads from bottom to top
maintaining means holding or keeping, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
the first letter of Gentlemen, two of them

explanation.surface: A theatre note: one Shakespeare play opened before Macbeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth sees a phantom weapon hanging in the air ('Is this a dagger which I see before me'), so the answer literally appeared before him.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's tragedy, a floating knife appears in front of the hero just before he murders Duncan.

clue.text: Memorial to a dental problem

blocks.note: first meaning: a commemorative tablet fixed to a wall
second meaning: the film of bacteria that builds up on teeth

explanation.surface: A monument raised to a toothache, as if commemorating it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a commemorative wall tablet and the sticky bacterial deposit on teeth that dentists scrape off.

clue.text: Pioneering leader favoured by fortune, being bold

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
someone fortune favours is lucky

explanation.surface: An explorer at the front gets lucky because, as the saying goes, fortune favours the brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucky describes someone brave and spirited, a close synonym of bold or courageous.

clue.text: Wild card held aloft by composer

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the letters run in a jumbled order
held means gripped inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
aloft means up in the air

explanation.surface: A composer holds a joker high above his head.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled card letters wrap around the word for aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Duparc was a French composer of the late nineteenth century, famous for his small output of art songs.

clue.text: Dog's dinner was made of the churchman

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
if the dog's dinner was made of something, the dog ate it

explanation.surface: A grisly tale in which a hound feasts on a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog's dinner' looks like the idiom for a mess, but read literally it says the dog dined on what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant to a parish priest in the Church of England, a junior clergyman.

clue.text: Holy box in second reincarnation

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
a reincarnation is a rebirth in a new form, so the letters take a new shape

blocks.note: a crate is a wooden box
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sacred casket buried in someone's next life.
explanation.definitionFit: Something consecrated has been made sacred by religious ceremony, which is what holy means.

clue.text: Ass in America leading to American kerfuffle

indicators.note: leading to means coming first, so the first piece stands in front of the next

blocks.note: in American usage the ass is the backside, or rump
US is the abbreviation for American, as in US forces

explanation.surface: A donkey in the States causes an American fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ass' looks like the animal, but American English uses it for the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance or commotion, the same as a kerfuffle.

clue.text: Indoor garden where wrath-filled politician loses head

indicators.note: something filled has another thing put inside it
losing its head means the front letter is cut off

blocks.note: wrath is fierce anger
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A furious politician gets his head chopped off in a greenhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party; once it is filled with the anger, its first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glass-walled building for growing citrus trees, a kind of indoor garden or conservatory.

clue.text: Take-off in second gear

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
kit is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: An aircraft leaving the ground in second gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take-off' looks like an aircraft leaving the runway, but here it means a parody.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch that mimics or parodies something, which is a take-off.

clue.text: Waspish, it might be, about Geller's unease?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: a jokey adjective: something waspish might be insect-like
Uri Geller is the celebrity spoon-bender

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a spiteful manner hides the famous psychic's anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waspish' looks like spiteful, but is read literally as wasp-like, giving an invented word that wraps Geller's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Insecurity is a feeling of anxiety and self-doubt, a state of unease about oneself.

clue.text: Exchanges lay classes to rest

blocks.note: with the closing words to rest, lay to rest means bury, which is inter
a course is a series of classes
completes the phrase begun by lay; its letters are already counted there

explanation.surface: Swaps that finally put lessons to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase lay to rest is split by its object: bury the classes, read in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Intercourse in its older sense is dealings or communication between people, so exchanges in conversation or trade.

clue.text: Hurrying up, grasping point of French adventure

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top
grasping means holding inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: apace means quickly, at speed
S is a compass point, south
de is French for of

explanation.surface: Rushing to grab a French point of view on an adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or reckless exploit, a bit of an adventure.

clue.text: Afflicted three bridge players receiving what they play for

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: the four bridge players are named after compass points; three of them are South, East and North
bridge players compete to win tricks

explanation.surface: A trio at the bridge table, suffering as they compete.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four seats are called North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stricken has been struck down or badly affected by illness or misfortune, so afflicted.

clue.text: Stout holy man, almost a holy woman

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: stout means plump or fat
an imam is a Muslim prayer leader

explanation.surface: A portly cleric is very nearly a female saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatima, the Prophet Muhammad's daughter, is revered as a saintly figure in Islam, especially by Shia Muslims.

clue.text: Begin to grow out of stupor

indicators.note: out of here suggests something put out of order, so the letters come out rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Waking from a daze and starting to flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprout is to put out shoots, which is how a seed or plant starts growing.

clue.text: Trade cards with one on ship

blocks.note: a hand is the set of cards a player holds
the Roman numeral for one
a craft is a boat or ship

explanation.surface: Swapping playing cards aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply places the one before the ship in an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicraft is a skilled manual occupation such as weaving or pottery, a trade.

clue.text: Make off with bits of deck and amplifier

indicators.note: bits of means only parts of the words are used, the ends cut away

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thief runs away with pieces of a hi-fi system.
explanation.walkthrough: A deck is a turntable or tape player; AMP is also the usual short form of amplifier.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly, which is to make off.

clue.text: Capital raised by Dior's original tunic

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word is lifted to read bottom to top
the original of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: Rabat is the capital of Morocco
the opening letter of the designer's name

explanation.surface: Money raised by a French fashion house's first garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless tunic, as worn by heralds or knights over armour.

clue.text: Knocks box over

indicators.note: over means turned back, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: to box is to spar, as boxers do in training

explanation.surface: Blows that knock a boxer over.
explanation.definitionFit: Raps are sharp blows or taps, such as knocks on a door.

clue.text: Student's record that's keeping back record

indicators.note: back means turned around, so the word reads right to left
keeping means holding inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a disc is a gramophone record
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A student's album that keeps a second album out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower or pupil who learns from a teacher, so a student.

clue.text: Invite approach, running after stream

indicators.note: after means coming later, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: a beck is a brook, a northern English word
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: Calling someone over while chasing along a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: To beckon is to signal with a gesture that someone should come nearer.

clue.text: A jolly girl in the fleet

blocks.note: taken as written
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cheerful young woman serving with the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like cheerful, but it is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, most famously the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Silver rouble accepted by representative

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so this piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for rouble
an agent acts as someone's representative

explanation.surface: A Russian coin taken by a sales rep.
explanation.definitionFit: Argent is the heraldic and poetic term for silver, from the Latin argentum.
